clues.text: This city stands on the River Thames, a wide river that flows to the North Sea. It sits in the south east of a big island in the west of Europe.
clues.narrowing: Rules out lands off the west of Europe and puts the player on the Thames, flowing to the North Sea.

source.quote: London stands on the River Thames in southeast England, at the head of a 50-mile (80 km) tidal estuary down to the North Sea

clues.text: The streets and crowds of this huge city trap heat in its dense centre. It can feel far warmer there than in the suburbs, an island of heat.
clues.narrowing: Rules out mild even lands; the city makes its own heat, so the centre runs warmer than its edge.

source.quote: London has a considerable urban heat island effect

clues.text: Royal clerks once rode from town to town with the king and his court. In the 1100s they settled for good here, and rule stayed put.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to old seats where a travelling royal court settled for good in the 1100s.

source.quote: the institutions of central government , which had followed the royal English court around the country, grew in size and sophistication and became increasingly fixed, for most purposes at Westminster

clues.text: Bright red buses roll over the bridges here, past black taxis with lit signs on their roofs. The red bus has grown into a loved sign of this city.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: red buses and black taxis with roof signs mark this city alone.

source.quote: In the decades since their introduction, the red London bus has become a symbol of the city.

clues.text: The United Kingdom is ruled from this city, by its parliament and its chiefs. Both have sat in the west end for hundreds of years.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: parliament and the national government sit in this city's west end.

source.quote: The City of Westminster, to the west of the City of London, has been the site of the national government and parliament for centuries.

reveal.blurb: Roman traders founded a town by the river here near the year 47, and it grew into a great port. In time the king's government settled here for good, and red buses and black taxis now fill its streets. London is the capital of the United Kingdom.
